In addition to the [[2026–27 Premier League|domestic league]], Arsenal are also [[Participating management|participating]] in this season's editions of the [[2026–27 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2026–27 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], [[2026 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]] and [[2026–27 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], the latter of which is their [[Arsenal F.C. in European football|41st European campaign]]. The season covers the period from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027. ==Review== ===Background=== Arsenal entered the season as the reigning league champions, having won the [[2025–26 Premier League]] title, their first top-flight title since the [[2003–04 Premier League|2003–04 season]].{{cite web |title=Arsenal end 22-year wait for Premier League title |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/news/4662306/arsenal-win-2025-26-premier-league-title-ending-22-year-wait-to-be-crowned-champions-again |website=PremierLeague.com |publisher=Premier League |date=19 May 2026 |access-date=8 September 2026}} Arsenal made significant use of set pieces throughout the season, particularly from corners, scoring 25 set-piece goals (excluding penalties), the highest total in the league, while also setting a new record for goals scored from corners in a single Premier League campaign, with 19. Arsenal's defence was once again a key factor in their success. They kept a league-high 19 clean sheets, while conceding the fewest shots (310), shots on target (90), big chances (50) and expected goals (28.5) in the 2025–26 Premier League season. Their average of 0.7 goals conceded per game was also the lowest among clubs in Europe's top five leagues. The 19 clean sheets were Arsenal's most in a Premier League season since [[1998–99 Premier League|1998–99]], while [[David Raya]]'s 19 clean sheets matched the club record for a single Premier League season.{{cite web |title=27 great stats from our 2025/26 Premier League season |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/27-great-stats-from-our-2526-premier-league-season-ageBS3l8XFZn |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=8 September 2026}} In Europe, Arsenal topped the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League]] [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League#Table|league phase]] with a maximum 24 points from eight wins in eight matches, conceding only three goals. After defeating [[Sporting CP|Sporting]], [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] and [[Atlético Madrid]] in the knockout stages, Arsenal faced [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] in the final, their first European final since the [[2019 UEFA Europa League final|2018–19 UEFA Europa League final]] and their first [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] final since the [[2006 UEFA Champions League final|2005–06 season]]. Arsenal lost the final 4–3 on penalties after the match ended 1–1 following extra time, despite completing their European campaign unbeaten.{{cite web |title=2025/26 UEFA Champions League |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/history/seasons/2026/ |website=UEFA.com |publisher=UEFA |access-date=8 September 2026}} For the first time since the [[2016–17 Arsenal F.C. season|2016–17 season]], Arsenal are without [[Reiss Nelson]] after the club terminated his contract by mutual consent.{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/reiss-nelson-leaves-arsenal-aK7qJ9T658rj |title=Reiss Nelson leaves Arsenal |date=27 Aug 2026 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=27 Aug 2026}} As a result of his departure, this is the first season that the squad does not contain a player that played under [[Arsène Wenger]], since before the debut of former captain [[Tony Adams]].{{cite web |url=https://www.mozzartsport.co.ke/football/news/after-43-years-last-link-to-wenger-is-gone-from-arsenal/68629 |title=After 43 years: Last link to Wenger is gone from Arsenal |date=2 Sep 2026 |website=Mozzart Sport |access-date=3 Sep 2026}} ===First team transfers (summer transfer window)=== The [[Premier League]]'s summer 2026 transfer window officially opened on 15 June and is scheduled to close on 1 September at 23:00 [[British Summer Time|BST]]. The window followed the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], which was held from 11 June to 19 July 2026, meaning clubs could complete transfers both before and after the tournament.{{cite web |title=Summer Football Transfer Window 2026-27 Latest News |url=https://www.premierleague.com/en/transfers/2026-27/summer |website=PremierLeague.com |publisher=Premier League |access-date=24 August 2026}} On 1 July 2026, Arsenal confirmed the permanent signing of defender [[Piero Hincapié]] from [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]], having activated the option to sign him permanently following his loan spell at the club.{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/piero-hincapie-joins-arsenal-in-permanent-deal-a64GQ9s3sBkl |title=Piero Hincapie joins Arsenal in permanent deal |date=25 Jun 2026 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=10 Sep 2026}} Hincapié made 39 appearances in all competitions during the 2025–26 season and helped Arsenal win the [[Premier League]] title. On the other hand, [[Karl Hein (footballer)|Karl Hein]] and [[Jakub Kiwior]] completed permanent transfers to [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] and [[FC Porto|Porto]], respectively, after their respective loan clubs exercised options to sign them permanently.{{cite web |title=Jakub Kiwior joins Porto on permanent deal |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/jakub-kiwior-joins-porto-on-permanent-deal-aIMXs2G4BAkI |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=24 August 2026}}{{cite web |title=Karl Hein to join Werder Bremen on permanent deal |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/karl-hein-to-join-werder-bremen-on-permanent-deal-aFY2l5G8E22L |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=24 August 2026}} On 9 July, free agent goalkeeper [[Illan Meslier]], formerly of [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]], signed a two-year deal with Arsenal, with the option to extend for a further year.{{cite web |title=Illan Meslier joins Arsenal |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/illan-meslier-joins-arsenal |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=24 August 2026}} On 15 July 2026, [[Leandro Trossard]] left Arsenal to join Turkish [[Süper Lig]] side [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]] for a reported £17.1 million. Trossard joined Arsenal from [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] in January 2023 and made 174 appearances for the club, scoring 36 goals. During his time at Arsenal, he contributed to a number of important moments, including scoring the equalising goal against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the [[2023 FA Community Shield|2023 Community Shield]] final and scoring a crucial late winner against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] during Arsenal's [[2025–26 Premier League]] title-winning campaign. He helped Arsenal win the Premier League title in his final season at the club.{{cite web |title=Leandro Trossard joins Besiktas |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/leandro-trossard-joins-besiktas-a2RJl0E1RyLJ |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=15 July 2026 |access-date=24 August 2026}} On 22 July 2026, Arsenal announced the signing of Greek forward [[Christos Tzolis]] from [[Club Brugge KV|Club Brugge]] on a long-term contract for £34 million. Tzolis joined Arsenal after an impressive 2025–26 season with Club Brugge, during which he helped the club win the [[2025–26 Belgian Pro League|Belgian Pro League]] title and was named the league's Player of the Season. He scored 22 goals and provided 29 assists in all competitions during the campaign.{{cite web |title=Christos Tzolis signs for Arsenal City]] in the [[2026 FA Community Shield|Community Shield]] final, winning the competition for the 18th time in the club's history.{{cite web |title=Arsenal 3-0 Manchester City |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/report-arsenal-3-0-manchester-city-axOZ78a0LKZm |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=16 August 2026 |access-date=24 August 2026}} Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring in the 23rd second of the match, making it the fastest goal in Community Shield final history, after being played through on goal by [[Myles Lewis-Skelly]]. A header from [[Kai Havertz]] doubled Arsenal's lead, with new signing [[Christos Tzolis]] providing the assist following a curled cross from captain [[Martin Ødegaard]]. Tzolis provided another assist for Arsenal's third goal, finding Ødegaard inside the box, with the Norwegian sending [[Gianluigi Donnarumma]] the wrong way with a feint before calmly finishing into the empty net. With his two assists, Tzolis became the first player to provide two or more assists in a [[FA Community Shield|Community Shield]] match since [[David Beckham]] did so for [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] in [[1996 FA Charity Shield|1996]]. On 21 August, Arsenal began their title defence with a 3–0 home victory over newly promoted [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] in the [[2026–27 Premier League|Premier League]].{{cite web |title=Arsenal 3-0 Coventry City |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/report-arsenal-3-0-coventry-city-an2Fq8x1O9cq |website=Arsenal.com |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=21 August 2026 |access-date=24 August 2026}} [[Kai Havertz]] opened the scoring with a composed finish following an assist from Riccardo Calafiori, before [[Bukayo Saka]] doubled the lead eight minutes later in the 23rd minute, calmly finishing in the empty net. [[Martin Ødegaard]] added a third in the 49th minute, with his shot taking a deflection on its way into the net, securing Arsenal's first three points of the season. New signing [[Christos Tzolis]] impressed once again, receiving praise from both supporters and the media.{{cite web |title=Christos Tzolis may have solved Arsenal's biggest weakness in bid to defend Premier League title |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/christos-tzolis-arsenal-coventry-b3037375.html |website=The Independent |date=22 August 2026 |access-date=24 August 2026}}{{cite web |title=Summer signing Tzolis continues to impress |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cvgjg3g0v1no |website=BBC Sport |date=21 August 2026 |access-date=24 August 2026}} Ten days later, on 31 August, Arsenal secured a 1–0 away victory over [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in the Premier League.{{Cite web |last=Coates |first=Live ReportingCharlotte |title=Aston Villa 0-1 Arsenal: Bukayo Saka scores winning goal for Gunners |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cr93ep2n2ppdt |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}} [[Bukayo Saka]] scored the only goal, sliding the ball into the net from a [[Riccardo Calafiori]] cut-back. [[Ezri Konsa]] also made his Arsenal debut as a substitute, becoming the first player since [[Petr Čech]] against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in 2015 to make his debut for a club against the team he had joined from. === September === On 6 September, Arsenal defeated [[Arsenal F.C.–Chelsea F.C. rivalry|London rivals]] [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] 2–1 at the Emirates Stadium in the Premier League. [[Morgan Rogers|Morgan Rodgers]] gave Chelsea the lead in the 2nd minute of the game, scoring the first goal Mikel Arteta's side has conceded this season. Kai Havertz equalised in the 25th minute, finding himself in a good position just outside of the box, before beating ex-Arsenal goalkeeper [[Emiliano Martínez|Emiliano Martinez]] at the near post. In the 50th minute, Christos Tzolis passed the ball forward, with Kai Havertz's clever dummy letting it go to captain Martin Ødegaard who slotted it in to give Arsenal the lead.{{Cite web |last=Reporting |first=Live |title=Arsenal 2-1 Chesleas: Martin Odegaard sinks Chelsea in London derby thriller |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/ck1wx0010el5t |access-date=2026-09-21 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}} On 9 September, Arsenal began their European campaign with a 0–1 win at [[Stadio Diego Armando Maradona|Diego Armando Maradona stadium]] against [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]]. Despite having 26 shots and 4.05 expected goals, Arsenal's only goal came from Martin Ødegaard's strike from the edge of the box, with Norwegian scoring his 4th goal in 5 matches.{{Cite news |last=Wright |first=Nick |date=10 September 2026 |title=Napoli 0-1 Arsenal |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/13582864/napoli-0-1-arsenal-martin-odegaard-goal-clinches-win-for-dominant-gunners-in-champions-league-opener |work=Sky Sports}}3 days after that, Arsenal traveled to the [[Stadium of Light]] to face [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]]. After a goalless first half, Sunderland were given a controversial penalty after Ezri Konsa pulled [[Dan Ballard (footballer)|Daniel Ballard]] to the ground. Despite that, David Raya saved the penalty taken by [[Enzo Le Fée]] and two minutes later, [[Bruno Guimarães]] scored his first goal for Arsenal. Then in stoppage time, [[Reinildo Mandava]] fouled Bukayo Saka and was sent off after receiving a second yellow card. Saka converted the penalty that followed, and Arsenal won 2-0. {{Cite web |title=Sunderland 0-2 Arsenal: Bruno Guimaraes haunts Black Cats with stunner after David Raya penalty save |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/13583579/sunderland-0-2-arsenal-bruno-guimaraes-haunts-black-cats-with-stunner-after-david-raya-penalty-save}} Then in September 15th, Arsenal heavily rotated the squad for the EFL cup tie away at [[Portman Road]] to face Ipswich Town and prevailed 4-2 with a brace from Max Dowman and goals from Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino. {{Cite web |title=Ipswich vs Arsenal LIVE! {{0}} }} |}{{clear}} ===Kit information=== This is Adidas's eighth year supplying Arsenal kit, having taken over from [[Puma (brand)|Puma]] at the beginning of the [[2019–20 Arsenal F.C. season|2019–20]] season.{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/adidas-partnership-extended-to-2030-aGKOZ1n8fT3k |title=adidas partnership extended to 2030 |date=30 Sep 2022 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2 Sep 2026}}{{cite web |url=https://news.adidas.com/football/adidas-and-arsenal-launch-new-partnership-with-2019-20-home-kit/s/a792ee1b-7f39-4f66-a095-a689e151ec5b |title=adidas and Arsenal launch new partnership with 2019/20 home kit |date=1 Jul 2019 |website=Adidas |access-date=2 Sep 2026}} *'''Home:''' The club revealed their new home kit for the 2026–27 season on 15 May 2026. The kit uses Arsenal's traditional colours of red and white. The shirt has a red body and white sleeves and is complemented by white shorts and red socks. Red shorts may be used in some away games when there will be a colour clash with the home team's kit. The shirt features subtle visual references to the [[Emirates Stadium]] to commemorate its 20 years as home of the club, including a bespoke collar inspired by the sweeping rooflines of the stadium.{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/the-inspiration-and-features-behind-our-202627-home-kit-a84jJ7T0sFDo |title=The inspiration and features behind our 2026/27 home kit |date=15 May 2026 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2 Sep 2026}} The kit was launched alongside a film named ''A Different Kind of Connection''.{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hGZSNVIhfBI |title=2026/27 Home Kit {{pipe}} A Different Kind of Connection |date=15 May 2026 |access-date=2 Sep 2026 |website=Arsenal F.C. |via=YouTube}} *'''Away:''' On 24 July, the Gunners released their new away kit, which reimagines the club's Bruised Banana away shirt worn between [[1991–92 Arsenal F.C. season|1991]] and [[1992–93 Arsenal F.C. season|1993]]. The shirt features an engineered graphic inspired by the iconic geometric pattern, which, alongside the shorts and socks, are navy with coordinated red and yellow detailing. The shirt also features the adidas Trefoil logo, which was previously used on third kits.{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/the-details-that-made-our-2627-away-kit-anvxx7n9cMEN |title=The details that made our 26/27 away kit |date=24 Jul 2026 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2 Sep 2026}} Yellow shorts and socks may be used in away games in which there are a colour clash with the home team's kit. A week after the launch of the kit, the club released a feature-length video that detailed the full story behind the Bruised Banana pattern of the past and how it was modernised for the present day.{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3VJZIaDM_YI |title=ARSENAL BY DESIGN {{pipe}} The story of the Bruised Banana |date=31 Jul 2026 |access-date=2 Sep 2026 |website=Arsenal F.C. |via=YouTube}} *'''Third:''' On 3 August, the club released their new third kit, which is inspired by the "belief, ambition and creativity" that defines the club. In addition to featuring the club's iconic lightning graphic, for the first time in five seasons, the shirt has the yellow base colour synonymous with Arsenal, as well as navy and burgundy details across the entire kit.{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/a-state-of-mind-details-behind-our-third-kit-launch-astD91N3aisk |title=A state of mind: Details behind our third kit launch |date=3 Aug 2026 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=2 Sep 2026}} The shirt is complemented by navy shorts and socks, whereby yellow shorts and socks will be used in the away games in which there are a colour clash with the home team's kit. The kit was launched with an accompanying video named ''The Arsenal State of Mind''.{{cite AV media |title=THIRD KIT {{pipe}} The Arsenal State of Mind |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FYmtqplffbE
